faq.heading: Frequently asked questions about digital maturity
faq.a1: Digital maturity is the extent to which a company uses digital tools and processes to streamline operations, decision-making and customer experience. It is measured along several axes: processes, systems, data, infrastructure, security and governance.
faq.q2: How does the assessment on digitalizuj.to work?
faq.a2: You fill in an adaptive questionnaire (19 questions for a quick screening or 50–58 for the comprehensive assessment). Based on your answers you get a DII-Compatible score, Operational Readiness score, AI & Automation Readiness, Technical Debt & Risk Index and Business Impact Potential with savings estimated in hours, person-days and EUR.
faq.q3: What is the DII (Digital Intensity Index)?
faq.a3: The DII is the official indicator of enterprise digital intensity collected by Eurostat across the EU. It scores the adoption of 12 digital technologies and enables comparison against the EU benchmark.
faq.a4: Partly — once you finish the assessment. Your individual answers stay in your browser and are never sent to the server. Only the finished result (calculated scores and recommendations) is stored, so you can open it later and on another device via the permanent link or QR code. No name or e-mail is stored — the result is reachable only through a random 64-character code that cannot be guessed. Traffic is measured via Google Analytics only after your consent, and the content of your answers never enters that measurement. A stored result is deleted automatically after 24 months, and you can delete it yourself at any time using the button next to the permanent link.
faq.q5: How long does the assessment take?
faq.a5: The indicative quiz takes 6–8 minutes (19 questions). The comprehensive assessment takes 18–25 minutes (50–58 questions with adaptive branching).
faq.q6: What is the mandatory e-invoicing requirement from 1 January 2027?
faq.a6: From 1 January 2027 Slovakia introduces mandatory B2B electronic invoicing via the Peppol network under the EN 16931 standard. The test checks whether your invoicing is ready for the transition and counts unpreparedness into the risk index.
faq.q7: Who is affected by NIS2 and Act No. 366/2024 Coll.?
faq.a7: The NIS2 directive, transposed in Slovakia by Cybersecurity Act No. 366/2024 Coll., extends obligations to thousands of mid-sized companies in energy, transport, manufacturing, healthcare and digital services. The test tracks NIS2 unpreparedness among its monitored risk factors.

methodology.heading: About the methodology
methodology.body: The assessment rests on two layers: the DII-Compatible Layer (benchmarked against the EU Digital Intensity Index) and the Operational Digital Readiness Model (actual operational digital maturity). Questions are adaptive — they adjust to your answers (Adaptive DAP model). Every score is auditable and can be decomposed back to its inputs.
methodology.intro: digitalizuj.to is a free online digital maturity test for small and medium-sized enterprises. In 5 minutes it measures your company’s level of digitalisation, compares it with the EU-27 average benchmark (Eurostat DII 2025) and estimates annual savings from automation — anonymously and with no sign-up.

share.privacyText: Your individual answers stay in this browser only. Just the resulting scores were stored on our server under this random code, which is how you can open the result on another device. Anyone who receives the QR code or link sees an anonymised summary and cannot identify your company from it. A stored result is deleted automatically after 24 months, and you can delete it yourself at any time.

impact.cumulativeNote: The three scenarios differ in how fast they ramp up to the full annual benefit — the dotted line marks the month when a scenario reaches its full monthly rate.
impact.whatThisIs: This figure is the savings potential from automating manual processes — computed from your answers about processes, maturity, company size and invoicing volume. It is not the return on the recommendations listed below and it is not a payback figure: the model does not know implementation costs and deliberately does not estimate them. Compare recurring fees (licences, backup, e-invoicing) against the annual saving, not against the two-year cumulative in the chart.

bench.estimatedNote: Eurostat does not publish medians by sector or company size. The comparisons below rest on our expert estimates calibrated to the Slovak distribution — treat them as indicative, not as measurement.
bench.microCaveat: Eurostat does not cover companies under 10 employees — the micro-company figure is purely an expert estimate.
